question_en: What is the name of the device in the image? Please provide the name and model code.
gold_trajectory:
# Detailed Simulated Retrieval Trajectory · P2-2-2-F01

## Step 01 · Identify device orientation from keyboard and panel text

**Action:** Observe the bottom row of ten numeric keys on the open portable case, the two large square keys in the upper left, the OFF/ON slide switch, and the STOP/START control. Use the search query "burst encoder ten digit keyboard recording replaying" to find images of old high-speed telegraph devices.

**Evidence Observation:** The panel has the words replaying, erasing, and recording; there is a connection section on the right, and the numeric keys are arranged in a single row. No brand or model can be directly read from the input. Do not fabricate details about tape mechanisms inside the case, contact counts, or operation steps that are not visible.

## Step 02 · Locate corresponding photos on the DÁVAČ page and in the manual

**Action:** View the DÁVAČ page on Crypto Museum, compare its historical photos with the image in the question, and then read the cover and title page of the attached TI-485 manual.

Device page, photos, and manual:
https://www.cryptomuseum.com/burst/davac/

https://www.cryptomuseum.com/burst/davac/img/davac_1.jpg

https://www.cryptomuseum.com/burst/davac/files/ti485_manual.pdf

**Evidence Observation:** The single row of numeric keys 1 to 0, the pair of large keys in the upper left, the switches, and the text sections correspond to the original photo. Page 1 of the manual preserves the corresponding historical photo; the title information on pages 9 and 10 links DÁVAČ with TI-485. The photos and attachments on the page belong to the same source chain and cannot be treated as multiple independent identifications.

**Result of this step:** The candidate name is DÁVAČ, and the code is TI-485; avoid misidentification caused by aliases within the same series.

## Step 03 · Compare similar panels such as MÉŠÍC and Speicher

**Action:** Prioritize comparison with the same-series MÉŠÍC, then examine the key layouts of other portable telegraph devices; do not treat them as having the same form factor simply because names or purposes are similar.

MÉŠÍC page and reference photos:
https://www.cryptomuseum.com/burst/mesic/

https://www.cryptomuseum.com/burst/mesic/img/302166/000/full.jpg

**Evidence Observation:** MÉŠÍC is also associated with the TI-485 / SIRIUS series naming, but its panel has two rows of recessed keys and two knobs on the left, which differ from the input's single row of ten keys and two large square keys. Therefore, shared codes alone cannot be used to identify the photo.

Speicher page and reference photos:
https://www.cryptomuseum.com/burst/speicher/

https://www.cryptomuseum.com/burst/speicher/img/302081/070/full.jpg

Speicher has two rows totaling 12 keys, along with indicator windows and recessed knobs; the layout does not match the image in the question. MA4010's central pointer-type component and three circular sockets, plus the lack of a similar numeric keyboard, make it only a functionally similar peripheral comparison:
https://www.cryptomuseum.com/burst/ma4010/

https://www.cryptomuseum.com/burst/ma4010/img/301834/000/full.jpg

## Step 04 · Retain name and code, end retrieval

**Action:** Return to the page and manual with the matching photo, and output the device name and code as required by the question.

The separately stored SIRIUS I materials in the question package can be checked for series background, but their content cites Crypto Museum and thus are not counted as independent evidence:
https://www.wftw.nl/30%20Sirius%20I%20v1%2000.pdf

**Stopping condition:** The panel structure corresponds to the original photo, and the name and code are determined by the accompanying documents; the answer is DÁVAČ; TI-485. There is no need to elaborate on usage descriptions or the device operation process.

## Final Answer

DÁVAČ；TI-485
